claimPolicy.correctness: Fovea passes every applicable hard check for implemented cache capabilities.
claimPolicy.performance: Every applicable Cache Lab L2 primary endpoint must exceed the preregistered dominance margin against every eligible comparator, unless a machine-checkable optimal-floor proof applies.
claimPolicy.scope: Inconclusive evidence blocks only its claim family; descriptive D1 metrics and L3 secondary diagnostics cannot create or defeat an unrelated L2 certificate.
claimPolicy.secondaryDominance: At least eighty percent of applicable secondary endpoints must be substantially superior and none may be materially inferior.
claimPolicy.semanticStratification: Only contestants in the same semanticGroup and durabilityLevel are ranked directly. Native PINCache results remain descriptive.
claimPolicy.unsupported: Non-common capabilities are reported separately and never imputed as passes.

disk.name: PINCache 3.0.4 PINDiskCache native
disk.operationQueueIsolation: Each contestant instance owns a dedicated PINOperationQueue that is drained at batch and teardown boundaries.

disk.attribution: The wrapper semantics belong to the Fovea benchmark harness, not to native PINCache.
disk.name: PINCache 3.0.4 with Fovea durable validation wrapper
disk.operationQueueIsolation: Each contestant instance owns a dedicated PINOperationQueue that is drained at batch and teardown boundaries.

completionBoundary.readThroughput: The timed read batch ends only after contestant quiescence; synchronous per-read latency remains the p99 sample.
completionBoundary.teardown: Contestant quiescence completes before clear, reopen, root deletion, or the next contestant window.
completionBoundary.writeThroughput: The timed write batch ends only after contestant quiescence; deferred work created by writes is included.

DISK-MIXED-V4.methodChangeFromV3: V3 estimated mixed-size p99 from only 192 first-pass reads, producing process-block ratios from about 0.20x to 10.93x. V4 retains the throughput pass and adds 1536 warm persistent-cache latency samples per contestant block.
DISK-MIXED-V4.p99SamplingBoundary: Read throughput uses one complete reverse-order pass plus quiescence. After that pass, p99 is estimated from eight deterministic rotated full-corpus passes; each synchronous API call is timed separately and every round is quiesced before the next. Extra p99 passes do not enter throughput duration.

hostExecutionPolicy.externalActivity: Build drivers are always disqualifying; standalone compiler/linker processes are disqualifying while actively consuming CPU.
hostExecutionPolicy.processIdentification: Use the full command executable token because macOS ps comm may truncate long Xcode paths; build drivers always disqualify and standalone compilers disqualify while active.

MEM-CONCURRENT-V3.corpusGenerationBoundary: The 1024-key/value corpus is generated before worker launch; throughput and p99 cover cache API calls, deterministic index selection and task scheduling, not payload or key construction.
MEM-CONCURRENT-V3.methodChangeFromV2: V2 generated keys and insert payloads inside the timed worker loop; V3 isolates the cache boundary and reduces non-cache allocation noise.

MEM-HOT-SCAN-V4.corpusGenerationBoundary: All scan keys, hot keys and payload bytes are generated before the timed interval; throughput and p99 cover only cache API calls plus loop/timestamp overhead.
MEM-HOT-SCAN-V4.methodChangeFromV2: V2 included scan payload generation and string interpolation in total throughput while excluding them from per-operation p99; V3 removes that inconsistent common overhead.
MEM-HOT-SCAN-V4.methodChangeFromV3: V3 declared twenty rounds but executed one. V4 implements all twenty fresh-cache rounds and aggregates all timed operations and latency samples within each inner trial.
MEM-HOT-SCAN-V4.roundIsolation: Each round constructs a fresh contestant outside the timed interval, preloads and visits its 32 hot entries, then times one 4096-entry scan followed by 32 hot reads. Keys and payloads for all rounds are precomputed.

sourceIdentityPolicy.legacyReports: Schema 2 and 3 reports remain readable historical evidence but are source-identity-unbound under the current policy.
sourceIdentityPolicy.researchEvidence: Dirty worktrees and edited dependencies may produce local research evidence, but cannot produce a trusted certificate.
